# Independent review of response-action evidence v1

Verdict: OBJECT for exact `134dea0df858000bdb3a2860d4c0f703ff1aef87` (Mote candidate `cand-0AGRN9FFCRDBTHW6XNHVQSFMX7`, issue `bd-01M31KPY7EK45HKWB9TJS1VFWJ`). Reviewer: backlog-worker-20260930. Fray #102. Base: b11d1909ac36bc4e732a1224605f1f90c5113798. Scope: the ten new files only. No candidate production or existing test file was modified.

## R1 - Medium: lossy UTF-8 permits distinct domain frames to share source identity

`modules/estimates/shared/src/main/scala/scalafim/estimates/ResponseBindingCodec.scala:16`, `:21`, `:26-33`; impact at `modules/fit-estimates/shared/src/main/scala/scalafim/fmri/fit/estimates/ResponseStatusScanner.scala:30-38`.

EstimateDomain.make accepts both `"frame" + 0xd800.toChar` and `"frame?"`. They are distinct admissible domain frame strings. ResponseDigests.features gives both the same digest: `efc8d98a05e00ea204b3d69fc81913cbc3f616ba9fa8889b5e08e641fd629f26` for a 2x1x1 grid and support [0,1]. Encoding substitutes '?' for the unpaired high surrogate, before SHA-256; this is an encoding collision, not a hash collision.

The scanner consequence is reproduced with the same revision, coefficient evidence and ordered support but these distinct frames. Instead of refusing the different feature identity before IO, scan returns Right(Scanned(...)), counting all five samples of the source whose frame differs from the binding. The two tests fail identically on JVM and Scala.js. The existing observation/column/schema/condition surrogate guards do not cover the domain-frame path. The refusal-only codomain still prevents positive scientific admission, but exact source/frame identity is not preserved as claimed.

Required repair: reject malformed Unicode at every native text-to-digest boundary, including domain frame and provenance strings, and ensure public binder/scanner boundaries fail with typed errors before reads. A validated lossless encoding alternative is also acceptable. Add a regression covering the feature digest and scanner no-read behavior; preserve valid supplementary-character inputs.

## R2 - Low: valid positive Int AR orders cannot round-trip

`modules/estimates/shared/src/main/scala/scalafim/estimates/ResponseBindingCodec.scala:240-242` versus `ResponseActionEvidence.scala:220` and the decoded-claim constructor.

Both binding and decoded claim admit any positive Int AR order. A valid FixedAr(1000000000, Global, None) claim encodes successfully but decode(encode(claim)) returns Left(Malformed("invalid number")), because Cursor.number allows at most nine decimal digits. Controls 1 and 999999999 round-trip. The failure reproduces on both platforms. The same parser is used by EstimatedAr.

Required alignment: support the full admitted Int range with checked overflow, or impose an explicit validated upper bound consistently at constructors and codec. Keep declared count bounds against remaining bytes and refusal of numeric overflow. Add boundary tests (999999999, 1000000000, Int.MaxValue, and overflow) for both AR variants.

## Verification and limits

- Independently reviewed all four new production files, external-access tests and relevant binder/scanner/codec/evaluator tests. The sealed five-case refusal codomain has no positive alternative; no numerical covariance or exchangeability proof is claimed.
- Fresh reviewer runs use the exact candidate plus two reviewer-local probe suites, with all production and proposed test blobs unchanged. estimates: 53/55 passed on each platform, with exactly R1 and R2 failing. fit-estimates: JVM 52/53 and JS 44/45 passed, with only the R1 scanner probe failing. Thus all 102 original JVM tests and 94 original JS tests pass; three added probes fail per platform.
- Added checks passing on both platforms: 13 Python-hashlib SHA-256 vectors at padding/block boundaries; all 720 permutations of six rows compared with an integer block-action oracle (exactly six accepted); 10000 deterministic arbitrary byte arrays return typed decode failures.
- Independently verified author log hashes, exit metadata, full test totals and warning-clean CompileAll receipt. Author checkout is clean at exact candidate. CompileAll was not needlessly repeated in this read-only review. Twelve staged providers used by the reviewer are tracked-clean; closure recorded separately.
- Known upstream JVM/JS structural-column identity drift and the White versus FixedSigmaT mismatch-label asymmetry remain explicitly disclosed. Neither is converted into positive-law qualification. Java construction trust remains a documented limitation before any positive version.
- First sandbox-only launch failed on sbt boot-lock access before tests; retained separately as infrastructure evidence. Both authorized reviewer batches exited 1 because the added regression probes expose the defects, not because of original-suite or compilation failure. No warning markers in authorized logs.

Reproduce from this isolated worktree (the probe sources are retained):

    python3 /private/tmp/scalafim-execution-20260929/run-sbt.py /private/tmp/scalafim-response-review-20260930 UNIQUE-JVM-LOG 'all estimatesJVM/test fitEstimatesJVM/test'
    python3 /private/tmp/scalafim-execution-20260929/run-sbt.py /private/tmp/scalafim-response-review-20260930 UNIQUE-JS-LOG 'all estimatesJS/test fitEstimatesJS/test'

Logs: `/private/tmp/scalafim-execution-20260929/logs/rae-peer-134dea0d-{jvm-authorized,js}.log` with metadata sidecars.

Manifest: `/private/tmp/scalafim-response-review-20260930/review-manifest.json`, SHA256 c3c420657bf1b2c2d47177ea13fd82734d778910943fa52d71fa78958262465f. The manifest binds candidate/base, all ten scoped blobs, reviewer probes, log bytes/actual exits and provider-closure location.

Next owner: phrf-claude-20260929 repairs R1 and aligns R2 in the owned candidate, then requests review of the new exact SHA. This review does not authorize landing or alter issue ownership/status.
